record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety. Let Hol(X,BU)^+ denote the Quillen-Segal group completion of the holomorphic mapping space from X to BU, where BU is viewed as the union of Grassmannians, so that holomorphic maps X → BU classify holomorphic vector bundles over X that are holomorphically embedded in trivial bundles. Under what conditions on X is the natural inclusion Hol(X,BU)^+ → Maps(X,BU) a homotopy equivalence?

evidence.quote: Let X be a smooth, projective variety and consider the Quillen-Segal group completion of the holomorphic mapping space, Hol(X,BU)^+, where BU is viewed as a union of Grassmannians. This space represents the "holomorphic K-theory" of X in that holomorphic maps from X to BU classify holomorphic vector bundles over X that are holomorphically embedded in trivial bundles. It is known that this

theory satisfies a kind of periodicity and sits between algebraic K-theory on the one hand and topological K-theory on the other. With the preceding understood, under what conditions (on X) is the inclusion Hol(X,BU)^+ → Maps(X,BU) a homotopy equivalence?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth projective complex variety. Let BU denote the classifying space of the infinite unitary group, realized as the direct limit of complex Grassmannians Gr_k(C^n) (over k and n). A holomorphic map X → BU is, in this realization, equivalent to a holomorphic vector bundle on X together with a holomorphic embedding into a trivial bundle. Let Hol(X, BU) denote the space of such holomorphic maps, topologized in the usual way, and let Hol(X, BU)^+ denote its Quillen–Segal group completion (with respect to the H-space structure coming from direct sum of bundles / block-sum on Grassmannians). The natural inclusion of holomorphic maps into continuous maps induces a map

    φ_X : Hol(X, BU)^+ → Map(X, BU),

where Map(X, BU) is the space of continuous maps with the compact-open topology. The homotopy groups of Hol(X, BU)^+ define the "holomorphic K-theory" of X, while those of Map(X, BU) define its topological K-theory.

Problem: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the smooth projective variety X under which the comparison map φ_X : Hol(X, BU)^+ → Map(X, BU) is a homotopy equivalence.
artifact.status_search_result: The comparison map between holomorphic (semi-topological) K-theory and topological K-theory has been studied extensively by Friedlander–Walker, Cohen–Lima-Filho, and others. After inverting the Bott class one obtains a rational isomorphism, and certain special cases (curves, P^n, some flag varieties) are known to yield equivalences. However, a general necessary-and-sufficient characterization of smooth projective varieties X for which Hol(X,BU)^+ → Map(X,BU) is a homotopy equivalence does not appear in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic K-theory, algebraic co-cycles, and loop groups
status_evidence.snippet: Cohen and Lima-Filho define holomorphic K-theory via Hol(X,BU)^+ and compare it to topological K-theory, proving the Bott-inverted version is rationally isomorphic to topological K-theory.
status_evidence.claim: The comparison between holomorphic K-theory and topological K-theory is known only after inverting Bott (rationally), not in general.

status_evidence.title: Semi-topological K-theory using function complexes (Friedlander–Walker)
status_evidence.snippet: Semi-topological K-theory agrees with holomorphic K-theory of Cohen–Lima-Filho; comparison maps to topological K-theory are studied with various partial results.
status_evidence.claim: General characterization of when the comparison is an equivalence remains a research question.
